links.outcome: LLM classification accuracy sensitivity to temperature, model size, and prompt examples
links.effect: Accuracy ranged from 51.9% to 70.2% across 12 configurations; 3B without examples had TPR of 2%; temperature effects varied by model size.
links.quote: The pre-trained models demonstrated varying levels of accuracy depending on the model size, temperature setting, and with and without examples ( Table 1 ).

links.outcome: LLM accuracy detecting stigmatizing language versus human-annotated reference standard
links.effect: Best configuration (8B, temp 0.25, examples) had 70.2% accuracy, TPR 94.1%, TNR 47.4%; many false positives on neutral clinical descriptions.
links.quote: The best performance in terms of overall accuracy was the 8B (largest) model with a temperature of 0.25 (smallest) with examples, which achieved an overall accuracy of 70.2%.

links.effect: Best model TPR was 94.1% but TNR was 47.4%; worst model accuracy was 51.9%.
links.quote: This model had the best overall True Positive Rate (TPR; Predicting “Stigmatizing” as “Stigmatizing”) at 94.1% although it performed the worst overall True Negative Rate (TNR; Predicting “Not Stigmatizing” as “Not Stigmatizing”) at 47.4%.

links.effect: Six no-example configurations were bottom 6 for overall accuracy, but top 6 for TNR.
links.quote: Of the 12 overall variations, the 6 models without examples made up the bottom 6, the worst performers in terms of overall accuracy, although they were the top 6 performers in terms of TNR.
